newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's July machinery orders.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's July machinery orders.

text.p: Japan's machinery orders rose a preliminary 13.6 percent in July from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, official data showed on Tuesday.
TAKASHI UENO, SENIOR BOND INVESTMENT MANAGER, BANK OF TOKYO-MITSUBISHI:
"The figure was much stronger than expected."

"The centre of market forecasts was around four percent month-on-month. Right now, the bond market will react negatively (to these numbers). I think the recent market has discounted various good numbers too much.

"There is little room for prices to go up higher. I think around the three percent level for the benchmark 182nd seems to be quite supportive. The current level looks very expensive to me. I believe the benchmark will be traded between 2.90 and 3.05 for the time being after the release of this figure.
"In LIFFE, there will be a lot of sellers after the release of these figures."
PETER MORGAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT JAMES CAPEL PACIFIC LTD

"It's definitely stronger than expected and suggests there is quite an upward momentum on capital expenditure related measures....(behind the rise were) strong orders in plant areas...This could be positive for industrial production. I think there has been a lot of negative sentiment about industrial production in the last few months because of the delay in the inventory correction process. But it's looks like that getting some momentum in these kind of orders will surely pick up production in the second half of this year."
